commands.review_summary:
Adds a core doctor legacy-config migration and tests to normalize `google`/`google-vertex` provider blocks by setting `api`, narrowing `input`, and backfilling `cost.cacheWrite`.

PR surface: Source +128, Tests +172. Total +300 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. source-reproducible: current main accepts the persisted legacy config shape while the model registry rejects the generated catalog for audio/video input, missing `cacheWrite`, and missing `api`. I did not run a live credentialed Google call in this read-only review.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] A narrow repair can move the migration to the Google plugin doctor contract, fix the mixed API guard, and adjust tests without a product decision.

target.title: fix(doctor): migrate legacy google provider config to current catalog schema (#102138)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102138. On upgrade, a `models.providers.google` block generated by an
older OpenClaw version passes the persisted **config** schema but fails the
stricter **model-catalog** schema. The whole provider is silently dropped — all
`google/*` models become "not allowed" — and any fallback chain that selects a
gemini model then hangs for 120s on the LLM idle watchdog.

Three schema divergences (all confirmed in source at current `main`):

1. **Missing provider `api`** — catalog validation throws `no "api" specified`
   (`src/agents/sessions/model-registry.ts:505`).
2. **`input` enum tightened** to `("text"|"image")[]`
   (`src/agents/sessions/model-registry.ts:165`); legacy blocks store
   `["text","image","audio","video"]`.
3. **`cost.cacheWrite` now required** (`src/agents/sessions/model-registry.ts:166`);
   legacy `cost` omits it.

The persisted config schema (`src/config/zod-schema.core.ts:382`) still accepts
`audio`/`video` and keeps `cacheWrite` optional, so an old block parses fine
then breaks at catalog load — a schema tightening with no migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a core legacy-config migration `models.providers.google.models-normalize`,
following the exact pattern of the existing `contextWindow-stale` and
`thinkingFormat-invalid` migrations in the same file. Under `openclaw doctor`
(preview) / `openclaw doctor --fix` (write), for `google`/`google-vertex`
provider blocks it:

- backfills provider-level `api` (`google` → `google-generative-ai`,
  `google-vertex` → `google-vertex`) only when neither the provider nor any
  model already sets one — never overwrites a user-set `api`;
- narrows each model's `input` to the supported `["text","image"]` enum;
- backfills `cost.cacheWrite: 0` when a `cost` object omits it.

Idempotent (a repaired block produces no further changes) and leaves all
non-google providers untouched.

## Evidence

### Focused tests — 19/19 pass (9 new + 10 existing)

```
✓ legacy google provider config migration > detects a legacy google block (missing api, wide input, no cacheWrite)
✓ legacy google provider config migration > backfills provider api, narrows input, and fills cost.cacheWrite
✓ legacy google provider config migration > uses google-vertex api for the google-vertex provider
✓ legacy google provider config migration > does not overwrite an existing provider-level api
✓ legacy google provider config migration > does not add api when a model already specifies one
✓ legacy google provider config migration > leaves models without a cost object untouched
✓ legacy google provider config migration > does not touch non-google providers
✓ legacy google provider config migration > handles non-record model entries without throwing
✓ legacy google provider config migration > does not match when providers is absent

Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  19 passed (19)
```

### Acceptance suites — 27 pass, no regressions

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/commands/doctor/shared/legacy-config-migrations.runtime.models.test.ts \
  src/agents/sessions/model-registry.test.ts
→ 19 passed + 8 passed = 27 passed
```

### End-to-end proof — real `ModelRegistry` catalog load

Ran the issue's verbatim legacy block through the top-level doctor migration
runner (`applyLegacyDoctorMigrations`), then loaded the block through the real
`ModelRegistry` (the same loader whose validation produced the issue's
`openclaw doctor` errors) **before and after** migration:

```
BEFORE migration → getError():
   Invalid models.json schema:
     - providers.google.models.0.input.2: must be equal to constant
     - providers.google.models.0.input.3: must be equal to constant
     - providers.google.models.0.cost.cacheWrite: must have required properties cacheWrite
   → find('google','gemini-2.5-pro') === undefined  (silently dropped)

migration CHANGES:
   - Narrowed models.providers.google.models[0].input to ["text","image"]
   - Set models.providers.google.models[0].cost.cacheWrite to 0
   - Set models.providers.google.api to "google-generative-ai"

AFTER migration  → getError(): (none)
   → find('google','gemini-2.5-pro') → gemini-2.5-pro, input ["text","image"]
```

The pre-fix `getError()` output matches the issue's reported `openclaw doctor`
errors verbatim; the migrated block loads clean and the model is available.
The secret-ref `apiKey` and `baseUrl` are preserved untouched, and re-running
the migration is a no-op.

### Static checks

- `git diff --check` — clean
- `oxfmt --check` — clean (also enforced by pre-commit hook)
- `oxlint` — clean

## Scope & honest notes

- **Overlaps open PR #102148**, which fixes the same issue via the plugin
  doctor-contract path but backfills only `api` + `cost.cacheWrite` — it omits
  the `input` enum narrowing (root cause #2). This PR uses the core migration
  path (structurally identical to the existing model migrations) and does all
  three fixes. Maintainers should choose one approach.
- Covers the issue's **first problem** (migration gap). The issue's second
  problem — fast-failing an unavailable fallback candidate instead of hitting
  the 120s watchdog — lands in the core model-resolution path and needs a live
  credentialed google repro to prove end-to-end; it is intentionally not in
  this PR.
- Migrations run under `openclaw doctor` / `--fix`, not automatically at
  startup (this corrects the issue's "hot-reload" phrasing).
- Scoped to `google` / `google-vertex`; `google-antigravity` /
  `google-gemini-cli` are out of scope (not named in the issue).
